name: Gadsden flag
description: A yellow field bearing a coiled timber rattlesnake on a patch of grass above the motto 'DONT TREAD ON ME'.
history: Designed in 1775 by Continental Colonel Christopher Gadsden and flown by the first Continental Marines and Commodore Esek Hopkins's fleet. The rattlesnake — striking only when provoked — was Revolutionary America's favourite emblem of vigilant defiance. The flag has remained in continuous use as an American symbol of individual liberty and limited government.

features.symbolism: the rattlesnake warns before it strikes — an emblem of vigilant defiance
